tagline: A stammering small-town boy who barely scraped through school scanned his office's lunch menus, built India's food-delivery giant, then handed the company to a friend he met at 15.
hook: In 2010 Naukri's founder Sanjeev Bikhchandani ran a WhoIs lookup to find who owned the Foodiebay website, then searched Google for Deepinder Goyal's name to find an email address. The ₹4.7 crore Info Edge then invested was worth about ₹5,000 crore on Zomato's first day as a listed company in 2021, roughly 1,050 times the money.

cast.name: Pankaj Chaddah
cast.role: Co-founder. An IIT Delhi batchmate and Bain & Company colleague who built Foodiebay with Deepinder in 2008. He said he had wanted to leave for some time but would not go while Zomato was struggling in 2015–16. He stepped back from day-to-day work on 31 March 2018 and stayed on the board.

cast.name: Albinder Dhindsa
cast.role: Deepinder's friend since a 1998 exam camp in Chandigarh, where the two boys sat next to each other. IIT Delhi mechanical engineer and Columbia MBA, he joined Zomato as head of international operations, then co-founded Grofers (later Blinkit). Zomato bought Blinkit in 2022, and on 1 February 2026 he became Group CEO of Eternal.

cast.name: Gaurav Gupta
cast.role: Joined on 22 June 2015 after more than ten years at the consulting firm A.T. Kearney. An IIT Delhi chemical engineer with a postgraduate diploma from IIM Calcutta, he was made a co-founder in 2019 and was head of supply at the 2021 IPO. He resigned two months after the listing.

cast.name: Akshant Goyal
cast.role: Chief Financial Officer. He joined on 1 April 2017 from Kotak Mahindra Capital and a fintech startup, and has been CFO since November 2020, through the IPO, the Blinkit deal and the move to profit.

founder.background: Deepinder Goyal was born on 26 January 1983 in Muktsar, a small town in Punjab. He was born into a family of academics, and his elder brother regularly outshone him at school; Deepi stammered and grew up feeling he fell short. He was a below-average student, and in Class 5 his father had to ask the principal to let him move up a class. When he later told his father about starting Zomato, his father doubted that someone from their background could do a startup.

journey.title: Born in Muktsar
journey.detail: Born on 26 January 1983 in a small Punjab town. His elder brother did well at school; Deepi struggled with a stammer.

journey.title: Nearly held back
journey.detail: His results were so poor that his father had to ask the school principal to promote him to the next class. He says he was in the bottom two of his class until Class 7.

journey.title: A lucky exam, then real work
journey.detail: An invigilator helped him in one exam and he came in the top three. When that teacher was transferred, he studied for a night before the next test and still came fifth.

journey.title: Meeting Albi
journey.detail: At an NTSE exam camp in Chandigarh, Albinder Dhindsa from Patiala took the empty chair next to him at the back. A year later they were together again at DAV College, Chandigarh, for Classes 11 and 12.

journey.title: From the corridor to IIT
journey.detail: At JEE coaching the two friends were the last names called for the lowest batch, and a teacher put chairs for them in the corridor. Deepi planned to skip JEE that year, got absorbed in his roommate's copy of HC Verma's physics book, sat the exam on a whim and cleared it on his first attempt. So did Albi.

journey.title: IIT Delhi, and feeling low again
journey.detail: He did an integrated master's in mathematics and computing. Surrounded by India's best students, he says, he felt low all over again. On campus he met Kanchan Joshi, whom he later married.

journey.title: Foodlet.com
journey.detail: Around his final year at IIT he started an online food-ordering site. Users did not come, and he shut it within a year.

journey.title: Consultant at Bain
journey.detail: He worked as a consultant at Bain & Company. Lunch queues in that office gave him the Zomato idea.

journey.title: Menus on the office network
journey.detail: Colleagues queued for paper menus at lunch, so he and Pankaj Chaddah scanned them and put them online. About 100 colleagues used it daily, and Foodiebay launched in July 2008.

journey.title: A cold email and a new name
journey.detail: After two years of bootstrapping, the company was incorporated on 18 January 2010 and Info Edge invested ₹4.7 crore in August. In November it became Zomato, partly to avoid stepping on eBay's toes.

journey.title: Too many countries
journey.detail: Buying Urbanspoon took Zomato to 22 countries. When funding dried up, it shut markets and laid off about 300 people, 10% of staff. He had hired many people he knew personally, which made it painful.

journey.title: Valuation cut in half
journey.detail: In May 2016 HSBC marked Zomato down to $500 million. He stopped talking to the press and did not read a single article about Zomato for six months.

journey.title: Buying Uber Eats India
journey.detail: On 21 January 2020 Zomato bought Uber Eats' India business for about ₹1,376 crore, paid entirely in shares, with Uber's stake capped at 9.99%.

journey.title: India's first unicorn IPO
journey.detail: Shares sold at ₹76 opened at ₹116 on 23 July 2021, and the market value crossed ₹1 lakh crore during the day. Months earlier he had given up his salary for three years.

journey.title: Backing his oldest friend
journey.detail: Zomato bought Albinder's Blinkit for ₹4,447 crore in shares, and Zomato's stock fell about 6% on the news. The same year he pledged the proceeds of his vested share options, about ₹700 crore, to educate delivery partners' children.

journey.title: Zomato's parent becomes Eternal
journey.detail: The listed company was renamed Eternal Ltd from 20 March 2025 because Blinkit had become a big part of its future. The Zomato app kept its name.

journey.title: Stepping aside
journey.detail: He left the CEO job on 1 February 2026 to chase riskier ideas outside a listed company, and handed it to Albinder. He stays on as Vice Chairman.

mindset.explain: He told YourStory the only effort he makes is to survive, because if you survive, you win. Every problem since feels smaller than the childhood in which he was 'not supposed to make it'.
He says he built a startup to get out of the rat race and chart a path where nobody compares him with anyone. He thinks comparison is a negative thing.

mindset.idea: Stay quiet when things are bad
mindset.explain: His lesson from 2015–16: when results are poor, nothing you say will be believed, so stop talking, do the work and let the numbers change the mood.

He has listed his own mistakes in public: people, capital allocation, product and countries he should not have entered. In 2024 he shut the Legends intercity service, saying two years of trying had not found product-market fit.

mindset.idea: A public company needs one focus
mindset.explain: He stepped down as CEO in 2026 because, he wrote, the legal and other expectations of a listed company's CEO in India 'demand singular focus', and his new ideas carry more risk than suits a listed company.

habits.detail: He still stutters on some syllables. Talking to people costs him a lot of 'calories', he says, so he avoids interviews and stages and spends the time on work.

habits.habit: Six months without reading about himself
habits.detail: During the bad press of 2015–16 he followed Sanjeev Bikhchandani's advice, stopped speaking to the media and read no article about Zomato for about six months.

In October 2024 he and his wife delivered orders in Gurugram in Zomato's red uniform. At one mall he was sent up the service stairs and made to wait there, and he publicly asked malls to treat delivery partners better.

darkestHour.title: 2015–16: 22 countries, then the cash ran out
darkestHour.story: By early 2015 Zomato had bought Urbanspoon in the US for a reported $50–60 million and was in 22 countries. Then investors stopped writing cheques. Zomato missed its targets, shut down several markets and, in late 2015, laid off about 300 people, 10% of its team. Goyal later said the layoffs were hard because he had hired a lot of people he knew personally. In May 2016 HSBC cut its estimate of Zomato's value in half, to $500 million, and the press turned hostile. Sanjeev Bikhchandani of Info Edge told him to stop talking and focus on the work. Goyal stopped reading anything written about Zomato for six months, held back on new verticals and grew the food-delivery business he had started in 2015. By 2017 he said Zomato had 150 weeks of runway and did not need to raise money.

genuineness.story: Before the 2021 IPO, Goyal wrote to his board giving up his salary of ₹3.5 crore a year for 36 months while still doing the CEO's job. In May 2022 he pledged the full post-tax proceeds of his first vested share options, about ₹700 crore, to the Zomato Future Foundation to pay for the schooling of delivery partners' children. When he stepped down in 2026, he returned all his unvested options to the company's pool for future leaders.

founder.now: Since 1 February 2026 Goyal is no longer Eternal's CEO. Shareholders approved him as Vice Chairman and non-executive director in a postal ballot that closed on 13 March 2026. His time now goes to riskier bets he started in the past year: LAT Aerospace, an aviation startup; Continue Research, which studies ageing; and Temple, a wearable that tracks blood flow in the brain. Temple raised $54 million in February 2026; pre-orders for its first batch open on 1 November 2026, with first shipments planned for early 2027.

milestones.title: Foodiebay goes live
milestones.detail: Two Bain consultants put scanned menus online in July. Within months it listed 1,200 Delhi restaurants.

milestones.title: Company, funding, new name
milestones.detail: Incorporated on 18 January as DC Foodiebay Online Services, funded by Info Edge in August and renamed Zomato in November.

milestones.title: Global, then into delivery
milestones.detail: The Urbanspoon deal takes Zomato to 22 countries. The same year it starts food delivery, which later becomes the main business.

milestones.title: Uber Eats India bought
milestones.detail: Zomato takes over Uber's Indian food-delivery business in an all-share deal.

milestones.title: Stock-market listing
milestones.detail: The ₹9,375 crore IPO is subscribed more than 38 times and the shares open 53% above the issue price.

milestones.title: Blinkit joins
milestones.detail: The board approves buying quick-commerce firm Blinkit for ₹4,447 crore in shares.

milestones.title: First profit
milestones.detail: In April–June 2023 Zomato reports its first-ever quarterly profit, ₹2 crore, helped by a ₹17 crore deferred-tax credit.

milestones.title: One bet ends, another begins
milestones.detail: Zomato shuts its Legends intercity delivery service in August and buys Paytm's ticketing businesses for about ₹2,048 crore; ticketing now runs as District.

milestones.title: Renamed Eternal
milestones.detail: The parent company becomes Eternal Ltd from 20 March. The website moves to eternal.com; the app stays Zomato.

milestones.title: New CEO, Blinkit in profit
milestones.detail: Albinder Dhindsa takes over as Group CEO on 1 February, just after Blinkit posts its first quarterly adjusted-EBITDA profit (₹4 crore, Oct–Dec 2025).

howItMakesMoney.summary: Eternal runs four businesses. On Zomato it earns commissions from restaurants and delivery charges from customers, and restaurants also pay for ads. Blinkit now buys and owns the goods it delivers in minutes, so the full sale counts as its revenue. Hyperpure sells ingredients and supplies to restaurants, and District sells tickets for events and outings.

failures.title: Foodlet.com, too early
failures.whatHappened: Goyal's first startup offered online food ordering in 2005, when few Indians were online. Demand never came and he shut it after about a year. He later called it India's first online food-ordering company and said 2005 was way too early.
failures.lesson: A good idea at the wrong time is still a failure. Three years later he started smaller, with just menus.

failures.title: Expanding faster than the money
failures.whatHappened: Zomato rushed into 22 countries using investor money. When funding dried up it had to shut markets and lay off about 300 people. Goyal later admitted that a couple of country launches should have been stopped.
failures.lesson: Every new market needs cash and attention. Grow only as fast as you can pay for.

failures.title: Legends
failures.whatHappened: Zomato's intercity service delivered famous dishes from other cities. It was paused in April 2024, relaunched in a new form in July and shut in August 2024; Goyal said two years of trying had not found product-market fit.
failures.lesson: Set a time limit on experiments and close them openly when customers don't come.

mythVsFact.fact: Only the listed parent company became Eternal Ltd, from 20 March 2025. The Zomato app and brand kept their name, alongside Blinkit, District and Hyperpure.
The website rebranded in November 2010, but the company stayed 'DC Foodiebay Online Services Private Limited' until May 2012, when it became Zomato Media Private Limited.

quotes.text: I was not supposed to make it, but I did.
When I told my dad about starting Zomato, he said, 'Janta hai tera baap kaun hai?' which basically meant 'You can't do a startup.'
quotes.who: Deepinder Goyal, at the Vishesh Sampark event (2024)

quotes.text: I started the first online food ordering company in India, ever. It did not work; 2005 was way too early.
quotes.who: Deepinder Goyal, in a 2015 interview quoted by Inc42

quotes.text: I did not read any article about Zomato for about six months.

lessons.title: Your first try can be too early
lessons.detail: Foodlet.com failed in 2005. Foodiebay worked in 2008 because it started with something simpler, menus, that people already wanted. If your idea flops, check whether the timing was wrong, not just the idea.

lessons.title: Start with the queue in front of you
lessons.detail: Zomato began with colleagues queuing for paper menus in a Bain office. About 100 people used the scanned menus every day before anyone invested. Solve a small problem for people you can see.

lessons.title: Grow only as fast as your cash
lessons.detail: Twenty-two countries in 2015 led to about 300 layoffs and a halved valuation in 2016. Before opening something new, ask who will pay for it if funding stops.

lessons.title: Shut experiments openly
lessons.detail: Goyal closed Legends after two years and said plainly that it had not found product-market fit. Saying 'this didn't work' early saves money and keeps your team's trust.

lessons.title: Friendships compound
lessons.detail: The boy who sat next to Deepi at a 1998 exam camp worked at Zomato, built Blinkit and now runs the whole group. Be someone people want to build with for decades.

factCheck.method: Researched from 39 sources, led by primary ones: Zomato's 2021 red herring prospectus (read in full from SEBI: incorporation date, renamings, Goyal's date of birth, salary waiver, Uber Eats price, team bios), Eternal's 2026 postal-ballot result, Goyal's own interviews (YourStory 2023, Business Standard 2016, Entrepreneur India 2017) and an extract from his authorised biography. Then independently re-checked claim by claim against the cited source plus a second source (Inc42, Outlook Business, Kotak Neo, Free Press Journal, The Week, TechCrunch, Forbes India and others); where a site blocked automated reading (YourStory, Business Standard, Entrepreneur India, NSE), the wording was confirmed through other reports of the same article or the search index of the page itself. Quotes were matched to the originals and one unconfirmed sentence was cut; the five video moments were checked against the chapter list in YourStory's own YouTube description; the three photos were checked on Wikimedia Commons for author, licence, subject and date. No free-licence photo of Goyal or his co-founders exists on Commons (a file named 'Deepinder.jpg' shows someone else), so only company photos are used.

disputed.note: Many profiles say his father, Harbans Lal Goyal, taught botany and his mother taught English, but these come from celebrity-biography sites. Forbes India (2010) says only that he was born into a family of academics, so we say no more than that.

Forbes India's 2010 profile says he struggled until Class 8, 'even failing class VI'. In his 2023 YourStory interview he described Class 5, when his father asked the principal to promote him, and said he was in the bottom two of his class until Class 7. We could not confirm whether he ever repeated a year.
Profiles disagree on whether he joined Bain in 2005 or 2006, and on whether he left in 2008 or November 2009. The prospectus says only that he worked at Bain before Zomato.

Zomato celebrates 10 July 2008 as its birthday (as reported by Business Standard and Wikipedia); Outlook Business says July 2008. Pankaj Chaddah has said he joined in mid-2008, a few months after Goyal began.

Goyal's 2010 blog, quoted by Inc42, gave two reasons: 'Foodiebay' sounded food-only, and they wanted to avoid 'overstepping' eBay once they took online payments. Inc42 calls this avoiding a possible lawsuit; we found no evidence eBay ever complained or sued.
₹4,447 crore in Zomato shares. Dollar figures vary: about $567 million (Business Standard) and $568 million (Inc42, Business Today); some earlier reports said $700–800 million.
Business Today says December 2013; The Week says May 2014.
Reports give adjusted EBITDA of ₹666 crore (Outlook Business) and reported EBITDA of ₹752 crore (Kotak Neo); these are different measures.
The 1,050x figure is at the ₹126 listing-day close; at the ₹76 IPO price it was about 633x (OfficeChai, quoting Bikhchandani's own data). It is a paper value, not cash.

Goyal told Business Standard in February 2016 that the layoffs 'had nothing to do with Zomato's performance'; in 2017 he admitted to Entrepreneur India mistakes in people, capital allocation and country launches.

'Unseen' (Penguin, 2025) was written by Megha Vishwanath, a Zomato executive, under an arrangement with Goyal. Business Standard's review flags this as a question for objectivity. Childhood details from it are marked as coming from the biography.
Inc42 calls the February 2026 round $54 million in seed funding; TechCrunch calls it a friends-and-family round at a post-money valuation of about $190 million.

YourStory's site blocks automated reading, so we could not open the interview ourselves. The Class 5 promotion, the Class 8 exam, the stammer, the 'calories' remark and the line 'I was not supposed to make it, but I did' are confirmed in other reports of that interview (Inshorts, DesiBlitz) and in search-index text of the page. Feeling low at IIT and the 'survive' and 'rat race' ideas rest on that interview alone, so they are given as his own account.
Forbes India (2010) confirms an elder brother who outshone him at school but does not name him. We could not confirm a name from a reliable source, so we leave it out.
